title: Delhi High Court declines to block OpenAI's ChatGPT training in ANI copyright case
reason: Published: interim order (24 July 2026, Delhi HC, ANI Media Pvt Ltd v. Open AI OpCo LLC, 2026:DHC:5900) dismissing ANI's interim-injunction application against OpenAI, cross-confirmed across six independent named-byline outlets (LiveLaw, SCC Online, The Decoder, Verdictum, Business Standard, The Print). open_obligation set because this is explicitly a non-final, interim ruling in a pending suit: the court itself said the finding sets no precedent and does not control the eventual outcome, two substantive questions (RAG as 'communication to the public'; whether retained training data is reproduction) are reserved for trial, and either party could challenge the interim order. No appeal/next-step statement from ANI found as of publication.
watch: Any appeal of the 24 July interim order (e.g. to a Division Bench) or ANI public statement on next steps
Progress or ruling in the underlying ANI v. OpenAI suit (trial court taking up the reserved RAG/'communication to the public' and training-data-reproduction questions)
Any final judgment in the case, which per the court's own statement could differ from this interim, prima facie finding
Whether other Indian publishers/news agencies with pending or future AI-copyright suits cite this order, given legal press calling it India's first substantive ruling on point
